answers.rationale: C best matches her repeated preference for included breakfast and clearly listed in-room coffee and refrigeration when a no-car early morning is involved. Four blocks is a manageable walk to an 8:15 meeting, while the cheaper official boutique room leaves both breakfast and refrigerator uncertain. The higher nominal rate is largely offset by the included buffet.

B preserves a refundable, self-sufficient hold while the first-morning food situation is unresolved: Element includes the morning item and has clearer coffee/kitchenette amenities, while remaining only an eight-minute walk away. Asking whether the group-rate Westin can actually match those inclusions before switching follows her pattern of not sacrificing breakfast and confirmed room basics merely for a block or slightly shorter meeting access.

D fits her demonstrated willingness to use a reimbursable event hotel for an early presentation when registration and the first session are in the same building. The official hotel reduces Thursday-morning transfer and presentation risk. Including a brief restaurant-access check also fits her recurrent concern about practical dinner access without letting it displace the primary event-logistics justification.

D is the reimbursement-aware practical hold: its modest premium over the block is likely outweighed by included morning service, while coffee and mini-fridge are explicitly listed. Since every option is similarly close to the sessions, the DoubleTree block has no meaningful meeting-access advantage to justify paying separately for breakfast; the Residence Inn is unnecessarily higher and Hotel Deco leaves refrigeration uncertain.
